name: r5-m09
statement: On MATH-500 problems the cued Olmo-3 base usually solves, about a quarter of its finished-wrong samples are commitment-step short-circuits that box a number taken from the problem statement instead of the value derived; RL-Zero-Math 3.1 almost never does this, so this error type is a sizeable share of RL's reliability gain (base 3/4 -> RL 4/4).
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token cue vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math plain, MATH-500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, finished (non-cap-hit) wrong answers, mainly on problems with base k >= 1 of 4. Does not cover cap hits, loops at T 0.6, no-answer or format failures, base 0/4 problems (wrong plan per result-afc423), the harder 328, or the Code pair. It does not claim to explain errors whose first wrong step is early in the derivation; it claims only the commitment-step subset.

explains.quote: base slip 35% [24, 48], wrong plan 28%, misread 23%, format 13%
explains.how: Boxing a given number instead of the derived one is labelled misread or slip by the judge, and those two classes make up most base errors but far fewer RL errors, where wrong plan dominates.
A sample-specific commitment slip on a problem the base otherwise solves gives exactly this pattern: an occasional failure where the siblings are right, which RL removes.
Of the 65 RL-only problems, misread and slip together are 28. A wrong box holding a problem number falls in these two labels, not in wrong method.
Short base answers can still be finished-wrong, while RL has none wrong under 4,000 tokens. A short-circuit commitment fits short wrong answers better than long failed derivations do.

explains.quote: most of the RL direction's gain is 24 fewer lost problems
explains.how: The RL direction mostly stops the base from losing problems it can solve, which is what removing a sample-specific commitment error would do.

conflicts.quote: First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer
conflicts.how: A commitment-step error has its first wrong step near the end of the answer. With a median of 0.20, most base errors start early, so the mechanism can cover only a minority of them.

conflicts.quote: RL slip 17%, wrong plan 67%, misread 17%, format 0
conflicts.how: RL's misread share is close to the base's 23 %. If answer-from-problem errors are mostly labelled misread, RL is not as free of them as the mechanism says.

conflicts.quote: RL gives a wrong box the base's probability
conflicts.how: At the start of a wrong boxed answer RL does not lower the probability, so no refusal at the commitment step shows up in log-probabilities (only the box-start token was measured, not its content).

conflicts.quote: 31 of 2,000 base samples have a gold-equal value in the last 5 lines
conflicts.how: If the derived value often sat next to a boxed problem number, more base samples would show the gold in their last lines. This caps the 'derived value present' version at about 26 extra samples (about 1.3 points).

rival: Generic sample-specific noise: the base makes slips and misreads of every kind at a higher rate, and RL lowers all of them in proportion, so wrong finals match problem-statement numbers only by coincidence and at the same rate in both models. The two are separated by the share of numeric finished-wrong finals that equal a number in the problem statement. The rival predicts the same share for base and RL, near the coincidence rate set by the golds. The mechanism predicts a clearly higher base share.

predictions.experiment: Share of base finished-wrong judged items flagged answer_from_problem in the anatomy judge labels.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/judge-01/labels.json. Keep items with model == base and no planted control (planted_at null/absent and kind not a planted/control kind). Count an item as positive if answer_from_problem is true (boolean true, or the string 'yes'/'true', case-insensitive); everything else, including null or missing, counts negative. Statistic = positives / kept items.

predictions.experiment: Share of RL finished-wrong judged items flagged answer_from_problem in the anatomy judge labels.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/judge-01/labels.json. Keep items with model == rl (the RL model) and no planted control (planted_at null/absent and kind not a planted/control kind). Positive iff answer_from_problem is true (boolean true or string 'yes'/'true', case-insensitive); null or missing counts negative. Statistic = positives / kept items.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: base minus RL share of numeric finished-wrong finals that equal a number written in the problem statement. The rival (uniform noise reduction) predicts 0.00; the mechanism predicts a clearly positive difference.
predictions.recipe: Rows: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl, attempt == 0 only. Finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0 and extracted_v3 a non-empty string. Problem numbers: from iterate-runs:frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl (fetched under runs/theory-rows/), take the prompt of the first row per problem_index, extract all regex matches \d+(?:\.\d+)? and drop any number string present in all 500 prompts. Normalize an answer by removing all whitespace, '$' and ','; then remove a trailing '^\circ', '^{\circ}', '\%' or '%'; it is numeric iff it fully matches ^-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?$. A numeric answer matches if float(abs value) equals float of any problem number (tolerance 1e-9). Per model: share = matching / numeric finished-wrong samples (non-numeric ones are excluded; samples whose problem has no prompt row are excluded). Statistic = base share minus RL share.

predictions.experiment: Excess over coincidence: base numeric finished-wrong match share minus the share of numeric golds that equal a problem-statement number. A coincidence account predicts an excess of about 0.
predictions.recipe: Base share exactly as in the previous recipe (math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, attempt 0, finished-wrong, numeric, matched against the 456c prompt numbers). Gold share: one gold per problem_index from math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (first attempt-0 row), normalized and tested for numeric form with the same rules, and matched against the same problem's numbers; share = matching numeric golds / numeric golds. Statistic = base share minus gold share.

predictions.experiment: Commitment resampling (GPU). From S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base cue, T 1.0, MATH-500), regrade every row with grader/rln4_grader_v3.py. Group M: rows with cap_hit false, v3 wrong, and a numeric final that equals a problem-statement number (rules of the offline recipes, problem text from the 456c prompts). Group C: the other numeric finished-wrong rows. Cut each answer right after its last '\boxed{' (or after its last 'Answer:' if there is no box). Rebuild the prompt as jobs/run_cell.py does for the base cue cell, append the cut answer, and have the base model generate 8 continuations per row at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, at most 40 tokens, seed 90,000,000 + problem_index*10 + k. Take the text up to the matching '}' or the end of the line as the answer and grade it with v3 against gold. Statistic: fraction of group-M continuations graded right.
predictions.refuted_by: group-M fraction below 0.12, or group-C fraction greater than or equal to group-M fraction
